check: Every scheduled or clocked person is on the roster
rule: every person id on a shift or a timecard matches exactly one roster row
evidence_required: the shift and timecard rows whose person id matches no roster row, listed by id

check: Every timecard belongs to one scheduled shift
rule: every timecard's shift id matches one shift with the same person, date and job
evidence_required: the timecard rows whose shift id matches no shift, or whose person, date or job differs from that shift's

check: Every scheduled shift has a timecard
rule: every shift on the schedule appears on exactly one timecard; only a scheduled shift is owed one, so a roster row with no shift is not a gap
evidence_required: the shift rows with no timecard, listed by shift id, and each person's hours summed from the timecards alone

rule: every timecard's person is hourly on the roster; a salaried row carries no rate and no timecard
evidence_required: the timecard rows whose person is salaried on the roster, and any salaried roster row that carries a rate

check: Every timecard rate matches the roster
rule: every timecard's rate equals the roster rate for the same person, compared in cents; a difference goes to a person, and neither rate is changed to make them agree
evidence_required: the timecard row and the roster row side by side with both rates as written, and the project lead's decision on which one stands

rule: no two timecards of one person on one date overlap in time; one that ends as the next begins does not overlap
evidence_required: each pair of timecard rows that overlap, with their clock in and clock out times

check: No person is double booked on the schedule
rule: no two shifts of one person on one date overlap in time, the same strict test; hours are read from the timecards, so a double booking is carried to the project lead and does not hold readiness
evidence_required: each pair of shift rows that overlap, with their start and end times and the jobs they were booked to

check: Hours are read from the timecards
rule: every hours value equals clock out less clock in, and a person's hours are the sum of their timecards and never of their scheduled shifts
evidence_required: the timecard rows whose hours differ from clock out less clock in, and each person's hours summed from the timecards

check: Readiness is a gate and not a pay run
rule: the check computes no gross pay and writes no pay figure; crew pay figures are prepared from the timecards only with the project lead's approval, and the decision matrix never lets AI send a payment to a crew member
evidence_required: the readiness result with no pay figure in it, and the project lead's approval before any crew pay figure leaves the studio's own tools
